title: Mueller v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied the complaint on the sole issue of whether the Redlands Community Church Session erred on January 14, 2019 by allegedly reaffirming its practice of fencing the Lord's Table contrary to BCO 58-4. The adopted decision held that the only relevant motion failed for lack of a second, so the Session took no action and could not have erred. The SJC noted the case could have been ruled out of order earlier, left BCO 40-5 recourse open, and made no merits ruling on BCO 58-4; a concurring opinion is separate from the adopted reasoning.
first_summary: The SJC denied RE William F. Mueller's complaint against South Florida Presbytery over the Redlands Session's fencing of the Lord's Table. The SJC held that the January 14, 2019 motion failed for lack of a second, so there was no action to review. It noted possible BCO 40-5 recourse.
summary: On complaint by RE William F. Mueller, the SJC reviewed whether the Redlands Community Church Session erred on January 14, 2019 by allegedly reaffirming its practice of fencing the Lord's Table contrary to BCO 58-4. The SJC denied the complaint: the only relevant motion failed for lack of a second, so the Session took no action and did not reaffirm anything. It noted the case could have been ruled out of order earlier and that Mueller could pursue relief under BCO 40-5; a concurrence stressed BCO 58-4 remains binding and criticized Presbytery's handling.
